focus: Frontier node F-2-008 (depth 2, scope OpenBot-main/api/openapi/learning.yaml, .skilled/skills): How does an OpenBot LearningProposal review (pending_review, approved, rejected with evidence) map onto a Skilled skill proposal?
noveltyJustification: 13 of 18 findings are new external evidence from the proposal schema, its review endpoints and the advisor's trust gate; 5 are new mapping inferences that reuse the needs-you item.
keyQuestions: How do the reference repos build bot memory (per-bot and shared) and skills (written, recorded from a demonstration, proposed from use), and how would those map onto Skilled skills and the spec-kit?
answeredQuestions: How does an OpenBot LearningProposal review (pending_review, approved, rejected with evidence) map onto a Skilled skill proposal?
ruledOut: Storing status as a field on the proposal
A new review command beside bots answer
Applying a proposal without the skill-advisor's trusted mutation path

label: LearningProposal requires id, runId, operation, status, title, description, reason, createdAt, reviewedAt and publishedSkillId.
LearningProposal.runId is the run that proposed it.
LearningProposal.operation is add | update | remove: whether it adds a skill, changes one, or removes one.
LearningProposal.publishedSkillId is the skill an approval published, null until approved.
LearningProposalDetail adds files (every file the skill would hold, each path and content) and insights (each id, statement and impact: what Learning noticed that led to it).
Evidence is a separate read, not an embedded field: each insight's evidence is read on its own from /settings/learning/insights/{insightId}/evidence.
Approve publishes the skill change to every Bot that learns there, approving again answers the same review, only an administrator may, and it is recorded on the audit trail.
Reject publishes nothing; rejecting again answers the same review and rejecting an approved one is refused.
Both review calls take an IdempotencyKey and answer 409 LearningProposalReviewed for a proposal already reviewed.
Skilled has no proposal mechanism at all: no proposals folder exists under .skilled/skills/ and no SKILL.md mentions one.

The one existing gate a proposal would pass through is the skill-advisor's trust gate: skill_graph_propagate_enhances is trusted only for a real apply write (mode=apply with dryRun not true), while report, propose and dry-run calls stay read-safe.

Four fields map directly: runId is the run record's id, operation is add, update or remove on a skill folder, files is the proposal folder's contents, and publishedSkillId is the skill folder name after apply.
status should be derived, not stored: pending_review is a proposal with no answer, approved is one with an answer and an applied skill, rejected is one with an answer and no applied skill.

The smallest proposal store is {stateRoot}/{identityKey}/proposals/{proposalId}/ holding the files verbatim plus one proposal.json, with a needs-you item per proposal so bots inbox and bots answer stay the only review surface.
Approve must be idempotent and reject refused after approve, which the derived state gives for free: a second answer finds the item already answered and returns the same review.

The one thing Skilled cannot copy is the administrator check: bots answer has no role check today, so on a shared host anyone who can run the CLI can approve; that is acceptable for a few people on one machine and is the first thing to change on a shared host.

direction: Store status as a field on the proposal
reason: Every value is readable from the answer and the applied skill, so a stored copy could disagree with them, the same failure the needs-you item avoids.
OpenBot serves evidence from its own endpoint so a reviewer reads it on demand; embedding it makes every proposal carry its whole transcript.

direction: A new review command beside bots answer
reason: The needs-you item already carries a question, options, an answer and evidence, which is the whole proposal review.

direction: Apply a proposal without the skill-advisor's trusted mutation path
reason: That path is the only write the advisor trusts, and a second write path would bypass its gate.
